name: Sports clubs, academies and turf/court rentals

problems.words: Two teams turn up for the same slot because bookings are on WhatsApp
quick_ideas: Keep every slot in one calendar owned by one person, so two people can't sell the same hour
Treat a slot as booked only once it's written there, so WhatsApp promises don't clash.

workzap_build.text: a slot calendar per court or turf with WhatsApp booking, instant confirmation messages, and double-booking prevention.

problems.ask_first: How many courts or turfs do you have?
problems.free_stops: Booking flow and slot rules per court go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare this week's double-booked slot clashes with the total slots sold, so you see how often chat bookings create overlaps.
Write every confirmed slot in one booking notebook kept at the desk, so staff stop selling the same hour twice.

problems.words: People book late-night slots and don't show
quick_ideas: Ask for an advance on peak slots, so a booking means commitment
Keep a list of groups who didn't show, so you know who to ask for an advance next time.

workzap_build.text: a no-show tracker per group with an advance link on peak slots, and freed slots offered to a waitlist straight away.

problems.ask_first: Do you take any advance for slots now?
problems.free_stops: Advance rules and waitlist handling are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which late-night bookings actually arrived this week, so you see which days and groups waste your best hours.
Give one staff member the late-slot callback list each afternoon, so empty night hours get refilled before kickoff.

problems.words: Slot advances collected by the ground boy sometimes never reach me
quick_ideas: Give players one account for advances, so money lands in one place
Match this week's bookings with money received once, to see what never reached you.

workzap_build.text: a daily match of booked slots against payments received, flagging gaps.

problems.free_stops: Matching rules and payment flow stay for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each advance noted for slots this week with what reached you, so missing collections stand out early.
Make one cash handover note for every advance received on site, so each slot payment is tied to the staff handoff.

problems.words: Academy parents pay late and I don't know who has paid
quick_ideas: Make one list of students by batch with this month's fee status, so you know who's paid
Remind unpaid parents once, since many simply forget.

workzap_build.text: an academy register by student ID number with fee status and reminder messages sent to parents.

problems.free_stops: Register setup and reminder timing are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count unpaid academy fees by batch at the same time this week, so you see where late payment is concentrated.
Keep one fee notebook by batch and let one person update it daily, so payment status stays clear for every parent.

problems.words: Coaches claim more sessions than they ran
quick_ideas: Note each batch's session as it happens this week, so there's a record besides the coach's word
Compare it with coach claims at month end, to see where the gap is.

workzap_build.text: coach check-in per batch with monthly payouts calculated for you.

problems.ask_first: Are coaches paid per session or salaried?
problems.free_stops: Check-in method and payout rules go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count sessions actually held this week by batch and compare them with coach claims, so disputed commission lines show clearly.
Keep one attendance and session log at the ground with one staff signer, so session counts stop changing later.

problems.words: Floodlight bill is huge and I don't know if late slots cover it
quick_ideas: Note lights-on and lights-off times against booked slots for a week, to see whether late slots pay for the lights
Check for lights running with no booking, since that is pure cost.

workzap_build.text: a utility log per slot showing cost against slot revenue.

problems.ask_first: Do you have a separate meter for floodlights?
problems.free_stops: How usage is logged and costed is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which late bookings used floodlights this week and which hours had lights on without play, so waste is separated from earning time.
Give one evening staff member the lights notebook and switch-off check, so unused floodlights stop running after slots end.

problems.words: Generator or lights fail mid-match and we give refunds
quick_ideas: List every failure this month and its cause, to see what keeps breaking
Agree pre-evening checks with your electrician, so faults show before the match.

workzap_build.text: an asset tracker for turf, nets, lights and generator with replacement dates and service reminders.

problems.free_stops: Asset list and service schedule stay for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note every generator or light failure this month with the match time affected, so you see which fault causes most refunds.
Assign one pre-evening walk round to one staff member with one fault list, so known issues are raised before players arrive.

problems.words: Students drop out after two or three months
quick_ideas: Ask parents of recent leavers why they stopped, to find the pattern
Share a short progress note with current parents, since parents who see progress tend to stay.

workzap_build.text: monthly progress notes from coaches to parents and alerts when attendance drops.

problems.free_stops: Note template and drop-off rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count leavers from each academy batch this season and note when they left, so the weak retention period becomes visible.
Give one staff member a weekly leavers list in one notebook, so follow-up reasons are captured while they are still fresh.

problems.words: Tournament registrations and fixtures are on paper and WhatsApp groups
quick_ideas: Keep one list of entered teams with fee status, so no team plays unpaid
Publish fixtures in one place, so the WhatsApp group stops being the record.

workzap_build.text: You would see tournament registrations, entry fees, fixtures and results in one place, with results posted to the team chat.

problems.ask_first: How many teams enter a typical tournament?
problems.free_stops: Setup details stay for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare paper registrations with group announcements before the next tournament, so you spot missing teams and conflicting fixture notes.
Keep one master tournament list with one person updating entries and fixtures, so matchday decisions come from one record.

problems.words: Night staff don't lock up or switch off lights
quick_ideas: Ask for a closing photo of lights and locks each night, so you see it yourself
Name one person accountable per night, so it doesn't fall between people.

workzap_build.text: a closing checklist with time-stamped photos and missed checks counted.

problems.free_stops: Checklist steps and timing are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many closings this week still have lights on or locks unchecked, so you see how often the miss happens.
Keep one closing sheet by the exit and give one night person the pen, so lockup gets finished before anyone leaves.

never_say: Training, injury, nutrition, heat safety or medical advice.
Collecting children's names, ages, photos or medical notes.
Investigating coach conduct with children; this goes to the appropriate authorities.
Advice on land, lease or permits; injuries on site mean emergency services first.

sample_reply.person: Ramzan mein raat ke slots full hote hain lekin aadhi teams aati hi nahi. Kya karoon?
sample_reply.pi:
Zaroor, ye sambhal sakta hai, aur is ke liye bade kharch ki zaroorat nahi.
Pehle, peak slots par advance liya jaye, taake booking sirf naam na rahe.
Doosra, na aane wali teams ki list rakhi jaye, taake agli baar faisla aasaan ho.
Workzap ye banwane mein madad kar sakta hai: whatsApp par booking ke saath advance link, aur khaali slot waitlist ko foran offer ho.
